title: The Empty Autopsy
premise: True-crime podcaster Bram Vane, who has quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths the police ignored, is hired by a nervous stranger named Cora Lindt to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the murder of her sister, whose autopsy file is already sealed, signed, and dated three days in the future. As Bram digs into the town of Hollowmere and its beloved coroner, they uncover a pattern: bodies whose autopsies were 'completed' before anyone died, all signed off by the same hand. The case Bram must close is one the town swore was closed twenty years ago, when a girl named Wren Halloway vanished and the file was quietly buried. In the end, Bram exposes the coroner's ledger of pre-written deaths — a protection racket turned killing machine — but only after Cora's sacrifice forces Bram to choose between the loyalty of found family and the truth they promised to tell.
about_author: Silas Brightwater is a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering coroners' inquests before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries in a drafty coastal house, accompanied by an ill-tempered cat named Verdict.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram Vane records the finale of a solved case in their cluttered studio, riding the quiet high of a third 'accident' proven murder. A stranger, Cora Lindt, arrives with cash in advance and an impossible ask: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. The emotional beat is wary curiosity — Bram has never been paid to prevent a crime.

chapters.title: An Autopsy Dated Forward
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Cora shows Bram the impossible artifact: her sister Maren's autopsy report, complete, signed, and dated three days from now. Bram's skepticism wars with the document's authentic detail. The beat is dread disguised as professional interest — Bram has seen fakes, but never one this good.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Welcomes You
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with Cora driving. The pair arrives in Hollowmere, a town too tidy, where Maren works at the clinic and everyone smiles a beat too long. Bram interviews Maren, who is alive, healthy, and unnervingly calm about her own future autopsy. The beat is creeping wrongness beneath small-town warmth.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Good Name
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Dr. Elias Thorne, Hollowmere's coroner for thirty years, is a local saint — he named a park bench after himself. Bram probes him gently and gets charm, deflection, and one flicker of something cold. The beat is the listener's trap: liking the man you suspect.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Signature
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, late night in a motel. Cross-referencing their three old solved cases, Bram finds Thorne's signature on every autopsy — deaths scattered across the county, all ruled accidental, all with pre-dated paperwork anomalies. The beat is vertigo: Bram's whole career has been circling one man.

chapters.title: What Wren Left Behind
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. Cora reveals her real motive: Maren's case mirrors Wren Halloway, the girl who vanished twenty years ago, whose closed file Cora's mother helped bury. Cora's guilt as a complicit family member surfaces. The beat is shame turning into resolve.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram and Cora break into the county records annex and find Wren's file: autopsy performed on a body never found, signed by a young Thorne. Someone has been checking it out — the logbook shows recent visits. The beat is the thrill of trespass curdling into fear of being followed.

chapters.title: A Warning in the Mail
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram's studio is ransacked; a cassette of their own podcast arrives with one added second of audio — a woman's last breath. The police 'helpfully' offer protection from a deputy who is on Thorne's signature list. The beat is isolation: the law itself may be the threat.

chapters.title: Maren Stops Answering
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. Maren misses work, then misses Cora's calls; her apartment shows a life interrupted mid-sentence, kettle still warm. Cora's calm sister was never calm — she'd found something and told Thorne. The beat is panic sharpening into guilt: Cora led the wolf to the door.

chapters.title: The Pre-Written Dead
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the signature list, Bram locates a retired nurse who confesses: Thorne ran a ledger of 'scheduled' deaths — witnesses, debts, inconvenient people — autopsies prepared in advance so no one ever questioned the cause. The beat is horror at bureaucratic evil: murder as paperwork.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fraying
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram's longtime producer Dee arrives uninvited, furious at being frozen out, and insists on helping; their argument cracks open why Bram works alone — everyone they've loved has been a liability. The beat is tenderness through conflict: found family chosen under pressure.

chapters.title: The Deputy's Confession
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee flips the threatening deputy by appealing to his buried conscience; he admits he signed off on two autopsies he never performed and gives them the ledger's location — Thorne's private mortuary chapel. The beat is a small redemption bought at great risk.

chapters.title: Wren, Alive Somewhere
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. A lead suggests Wren Halloway didn't die — she ran, and Thorne has kept her 'death' closed ever since. Cora realizes Maren may be held where Wren once hid. The beat is desperate hope: the closed case was closed to hide a living witness.

chapters.title: The Mortuary Chapel
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram and Dee infiltrate the chapel and find the ledger — decades of scheduled deaths, Maren's page fresh ink — but trip a silent alarm. They escape with photographs as Thorne's people close in. The beat is triumph one breath ahead of catastrophe.

chapters.title: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, dawn. The chapel burns overnight; the ledger's original is ash, and the deputy is found dead — an autopsy already on file, dated yesterday. Bram realizes the fire was scheduled too. The beat is grief and fury: evidence destroyed, a friend's source silenced.

chapters.title: Thorne Invites Bram to Tea
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Thorne, unafraid, invites Bram to his home, offering partnership: Bram's reach, his method — together they could 'curate' justice. He reveals he knows everything about Bram's three cases, and about Dee and Cora. The beat is seductive corruption: the villain makes a horrifying kind of sense.

chapters.title: What Bram Almost Signed
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, intimate and quiet. Tempted by protection for Dee and Cora, Bram nearly accepts — then finds Wren's name in a digitized fragment of the ledger, marked not 'scheduled' but 'witness, retained.' The beat is the moral hinge: loyalty to the living versus the truth owed to the erased.

chapters.title: The Retained Witness
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. Following the fragment, Cora finds Wren Halloway alive — elderly, hidden, complicit in her own erasure to survive. Wren gives them the one thing fire couldn't destroy: her memory, recorded. The beat is the price of survival made flesh: she lived by letting the lie stand.

chapters.title: Broadcast Live from Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Knowing Thorne will kill Maren once the heat dies, Bram does the unthinkable: airs everything live — ledger pages, Wren's testimony, the pre-dated autopsies — making the town itself the witness no one can bury. The beat is all-in courage: truth as the only shield.

chapters.title: The Chapel Basement
chapters.summary: Bram and Cora's alternating POV. While the town erupts, Bram and Cora race to the chapel basement where Maren is held; Thorne waits, calm, offering Bram one last trade. Cora takes a bullet meant for Bram. The beat is the climax: loyalty and truth finally pointing the same direction, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Empty Autopsy
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Thorne is arrested as the state audit unravels his ledger; Maren's autopsy is formally voided — an empty file at last. Cora survives, changed. Bram records the final episode, naming Wren and the dead aloud. The beat is catharsis: a closed case reopened, then truly closed.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue. Months later, Bram and Dee rebuild the podcast as a collective with Cora and Maren aboard; Wren attends her own belated memorial, finally allowed to grieve herself. Bram visits the first grave they ever reopened. The beat is bittersweet peace: survival has a price, but truth is how the living pay it forward.
